item.description: ### Fixed - **Perch no longer removes hooks of yours that only mention it.** A hook or status line counted as Perch's whenever its command contained the name of one of Perch's helpers — so something like `check-policy --log /tmp/perch-report.log` was deleted when Perch updated its hooks, on Remove Integration, and by the uninstaller. Perch now claims only commands in the exact shape it writes, and leaves everything else alone. - **Codex: Stop is offered only when Perch can see Codex's approval prompts.** Pressing Escape at a Codex approval prompt denies it, so Stop needs proof that Perch's approval hook is installed, switched on and trusted in Codex. Perch now asks Codex itself, re-checks whenever Codex's hook or config files change, and keeps Stop off until Codex confirms — usually about a second. - **Codex: replies get the same check.** A reply typed into a Codex approval prompt approves the command, so replies to Codex sessions now also wait for Codex to confirm Perch's approval hook. A Codex session started with `--disable hooks` or `-c features.hooks=false` shows "no hooks" and offers no replies or Stop. Codex sessions in Codex's background service no longer take replies through herdr either; start Codex with `--no-daemon` to get them.
